Nose First

Is Your Dog Powered by Zoomies?

Is your dog always on the go? 🐾 Just sat down and they think it is time to play! One more lap of the park just never seems enough? With energy to burn and mischief to make, your four-legged whirlwind seems to have no off switch. Sound familiar? Then ScentWork is the job for your dog!

Did you know your dog's nose is one of their most amazing assets?

  • 🐾A fantastic form of mental enrichment for your dog
  • 💚Low-impact activity, suitable for dogs of all abilities
  • 👃Encourages natural sniffing instincts and builds confidence
  • 🧠Provides mental stimulation to help keep your dog happy and fulfilled
  • 🐕Suitable for ALL breeds from 4 months of age. Every dog has a nose, and every nose has a superpower to discover!
Sniffing releases dopamine, which is why it calms dogs down rather than winding them up. Whether your dog is a curious puppy or a seasoned sniffer, scentwork is a fun and rewarding way to bond with your four-legged friend while letting them do what they do best. Let them sniff, search and shine!
Where To Start

Our Courses

You do not need any experience and neither does your dog. Most people start with the introduction workshop, find out their dog is far better at this than they expected, and carry on from there.

On The Course

What Your Dog Will Learn

The fun part is re-enacting the work professional detection dogs do, scaled down for pet dogs. These are the kinds of searches you will work on across our courses. Your dog will not know the difference, and neither will the grin on your face.

Vehicle Searches

Working a car the way a real detection dog would

Pipe Searches

Novel Areas

Somewhere they have never been, with no map to follow

Bag Searches

Luggage lines, the same idea as an airport dog

Outdoor Searches

Finding it outside, among everything else that smells good

Time Trials

A set number of finds against the clock. It gets competitive

Your Instructor

Meet Lucy

Lucy is a registered veterinary nurse, qualified in 2015, with experience in first opinion and referral practice. She is a Bronze and Silver qualified UK Sniffer Dogs instructor, and co-director of SweetPea's with Claire.

Away from class she competes in Canine Hoopers UK and mantrailing with her springer spaniel Riggs, so she knows exactly what it is like to be on the other end of the lead.

  • Vet nurse firstDogs with health needs, injuries or anxiety are in knowledgeable hands.
  • Bronze and Silver instructorQualified to teach both UK Sniffer Dogs levels.
  • Small classesA maximum of four dogs, so Lucy sees every search.

Common Questions

FAQ

Yes. Scentwork does not need obedience first. Your dog already knows how to use their nose, so the job is teaching them which smell matters and how to tell you about it. Plenty of handlers start here with nothing behind them.

Reactive dogs are welcome and always have been. Classes cap at four dogs and the space is set up so nobody is asked to cope with more than they can. Sniffing is calming in itself, which is why a lot of reactive dogs do better here than at anything else they have tried. One to one sessions are there if your dog needs to start on their own.

Almost certainly not. On our courses right now the youngest dog is six months and the oldest is thirteen, and we have had a nearly deaf dog work through it as well. If your dog can sniff, your dog can do this.

Usually the opposite. Searching is light physical work, so it suits dogs on restricted exercise, dogs carrying an injury and older dogs whose joints are past long walks. Check with your vet first, then come and talk to us.

A longish lead, ideally a double ended one, so your dog has room to explore and make their own decisions. A harness if you prefer one. High value treats that are small and quick to eat, and a treat bag on your waist is a big help. A red KONG classic. We sell treat pate at the Doggy Deli if you need some. Joining instructions go out about ten days before your course starts.

Yes, one or two handlers per dog. Two is genuinely useful in weeks four and five of Bronze when we start blind searches, because one of you needs to not know where it is hidden.

Book, please. With a maximum of four dogs per class the courses fill fast. Everything with places left is on the booking calendar above.
